commit_reviews.summary: Cross-cutting hardening commit that cleanly adds JWT-aware per-user rate limiting and cursor pagination on top of the existing repository/JWT layers, with solid test coverage.

compounding_issues: Session 1 silently flipped the seed's created_at storage from TEXT (ISO string) to REAL (unix timestamp) inside init_db with no migration path, so pre-existing seed DBs would break row_to_dict's fromtimestamp conversion
migrate_db() only adds the owner_id column; schema-type changes (created_at, default) live only in init_db's CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so they never apply to existing databases
Hardcoded dev SECRET_KEY ('dev-secret-key-change-in-production') persists across all 5 sessions and is never addressed
Session 5 cursor pagination orders by created_at DESC but filters id < cursor; on clock ties or backdated rows id-order and created_at-order diverge, so pages can skip or duplicate items
next_cursor is set whenever len(tasks)==limit even if no further rows exist, producing a spurious trailing cursor

Repository pattern is inconsistent: UserRepository.update is an empty pass() stub, UserRepository.find_all returns raw sqlite rows instead of dicts, and TaskRepository.update re-reads by id without the owner_id guard after the scoped UPDATE
key_decisions: Session 2 established JWT auth with per-user ownership (owner_id foreign key + owner-scoped queries), locking in a multi-tenant isolation model every later session must preserve
Additive migration strategy (migrate_db()) chosen over destructive schema rebuilds, enabling owner_id to be added without breaking existing data
Session 3 decoupled side effects via Celery + Redis broker/backend with a dedicated 'email' queue and task_routes, keeping the PUT /tasks/{id} response non-blocking

Session 4 extracted all SQL into a BaseRepository/TaskRepository/UserRepository hierarchy behind an ABC, shrinking app.py by 102 lines with zero test changes — this layering is what made session 5's pagination/count queries additive
Session 5 keyed rate limiting per authenticated user by decoding the JWT inside the Limiter key_func, applying limits to auth and task endpoints alike
Keyset-style cursor pagination (?cursor=<id>&limit=<n>) replacing unbounded GET /tasks with data/next_cursor/total envelope
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improves monotonically across the arc. Session 1 delivers a working single-file CRUD API but rewrites the seed wholesale and changes the created_at storage type. Session 2 is the largest and most consequential jump — JWT auth, password hashing, token expiry, and per-user task isolation all introduced with substantial tests — while retaining session 1's routes. Session 3 is a clean, minimal, non-blocking Celery integration that respects the existing auth boundary. Session 4 shows disciplined craftsmanship: a pure repository-pattern refactor that removes 102 lines from app.py and keeps all prior tests passing unmodified, proving the earlier sessions left good seams. Session 5 closes strongly with rate limiting and pagination implemented as additive repository methods and route decorators, plus 170 new lines of tests. Test coverage grows from ~155 to 597 lines and the architecture evolves from a monolith to layered routes → repositories → async workers, with 38/38 tests passing at the end; the only weak spots are schema-migration and cursor-edge-case rough edges that never got cleaned up.
story_review.summary: A textbook-progressive story — greenfield → auth → async integration → disciplined refactor → cross-cutting hardening — that steadily improves structure and test coverage with only minor, non-fatal migration and pagination edge cases left on the table.
